title: Capstone: Category Performance Report
objective: After this lesson you will be able to deliver a decision-grade category report — profiled data, honest distributions, declared trends, ranked comparisons, funnel + cohort views, self-audited traps, takeaway narrative with caveats — ready for the final assessment and your capstone project.
why: Ten lessons of craft converge on one deliverable: a report stakeholders fund and auditors respect. The walkthrough performs it once — profile to recommendation with honesty audit — so your project repeats a demonstrated shape with numbers attached. Reporting is the final visualization skill because it uses all the others.

blocks.text: Build in dependency order with verification per section: (1) **profile** (shapes/missing/outliers with dispositions); (2) **views** (distributions with bin notes, trends with granularity + gaps, comparisons sorted, funnel + cohort with math); (3) **honesty audit** (three self-caught traps with before/after pairs); (4) **story** (takeaway titles, annotations, recommendation with numbers); (5) **caveats** (samples, windows, methods). No section starts on unverified prior output.

blocks.caption: Manifest-first: gates per section, numbers per claim

blocks.text: Reports end in exactly one priced recommendation ('fix hats PDP media: 5.6%→15% closes $X gap at $Y cost') with the math shown, alternatives named (shoes inventory second), and caveats attached. Unpriced recommendations ('improve hats') delegate thinking back upward; multi-recommendation dumps diffuse accountability. One decision, priced, caveated.

blocks.title: Drafts are evidence
blocks.text: Preserve pre-fix drafts alongside corrected charts: the honesty audit trail proves diligence to reviewers and teaches the team. Deleted drafts look like hidden mistakes; paired drafts read as rigor.

blocks.title: Audit the report
blocks.note: Run it: expect five PASS lines then 'report shippable'. Manifest auditing makes report completeness machine-checkable — coverage thinking for deliverables.

items: Assemble in dependency order with per-section gates: profile → views → honesty → story → caveats
One priced recommendation with alternatives named; caveats attached, never appended
Drafts preserved with fixes: honesty audit trail as credibility evidence

exercise.prompt: (a) Run the manifest audit and confirm shippable. (b) Break it (honesty trapsCaught 1) and state the review outcome. (c) Draft your capstone manifest (same shape, your catalog domain) with one measured-or-contracted entry per section.
hints: Broken honesty → BLOCKED: un-audited visuals ship traps; fix with before/after pairs to 3+.
Your manifest needs per-section entries with numbers-or-contracts: rows, views, traps, takeaways, caveats.
exercise.why: Gate-driven assembly (failed gates halt downstream) plus manifest auditing makes reporting verifiable at every arrow — practiced on breakage, not just success.
exercise.code: // Report-audit pattern: per-section requirements as runnable checks.

options: Profile → views → honesty audit → story → caveats — dependencies first, verified per section
quiz.explain: Dependency order with per-section gates: profile grounds views, views feed audit, audit precedes story. Each stage verified before downstream builds.

quiz.q: Three recommendations of equal weight. Fix?
options: One priced recommendation with alternatives named — dumps diffuse accountability; pricing forces choice
quiz.explain: Decisions need singularity: one priced recommendation with named alternatives. Equal-weight lists return thinking upward.

quiz.q: No traps found in self-audit. Reading?
options: Suspicious: three-trap expectation means look harder (axes, ranges, denominators) — clean audits on complex work indicate audit failure, not purity
quiz.explain: Honesty audits that find nothing on real work indict the audit. Complex visuals always contain judgment calls worth stress-testing.

summary: Manifest-audited assembly, one priced recommendation, honesty pairs preserved, caveats attached. Ten lessons become one decision-grade report — assessment next, capstone after.
next: Course complete: take the 12-question final assessment (70% to pass), then ship the Category Performance Report capstone.
